must_read.text: Thick disks ($h/r \sim 0.3$) achieve the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state ($\phi_{\rm BH} = 50$) by $t \simeq 2\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ with electromagnetic jet efficiency $\eta_{\rm EM} \ge 100\%$, whereas thinner disks fail to reach MAD within comparable runtimes, giving $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 5$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.1$) for $h/r=0.2$ and $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 3\times 10^{-2}$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.01$) for $h/r=0.1$.

highlights.title: Thinner Disks Struggle to Launch Jets: GRMHD Simulations of Magnetic Field Generation and Transport
highlights.reason: This work directly addresses the physical mechanism of magnetic flux generation, transport, and relativistic jet launching in black hole accretion systems across varying disk thicknesses ($h/r=0.1$--$0.3$) using 3D GRMHD simulations, providing crucial scaling relations for MAD formation timescales and jet power relevant to GRBs, TDEs, and high-energy transients.

highlights.title: Extreme eccentricity in double neutron stars without exotic physics
highlights.reason: This paper presents a definitive orbital dynamics and evolutionary model explaining the origin of the record-breaking eccentric double neutron star PSR J0653+0443 within standard isolated binary evolution without requiring exotic dynamical channels.

highlights.title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
highlights.reason: The paper provides public r-process nucleosynthesis yields and tracer trajectories from numerical relativity BNS merger simulations with long-lived remnants and M1 neutrino transport, directly relevant to kilonova physics and heavy element nucleosynthesis.

highlights.title: Considering Numerical Relativity Surrogate Models for AGN Channel Merger Dynamics
highlights.reason: The paper benchmarks numerical relativity surrogate models against analytic approximations within the McFACTS framework for AGN disk-assisted hierarchical binary black hole mergers, directly informing compact object retention, kick distributions, and high-energy merger environments.

highlights.title: Validating an X-ray-based method for identifying Fermi blazars
highlights.reason: The paper provides an observational validation of an X-ray-based identification technique for Fermi unidentified gamma-ray sources (UGSs), testing counterpart association with relativistic jets (BL Lacs and gamma-ray Seyferts). This informs multi-wavelength counterparts and relativistic jet associations for high-energy transient and gamma-ray catalogs.

highlights.title: Search for Eccentric Neutron Star-Black Hole Binaries in Advanced LIGO's Fourth Observing Run using Effective-One-Body Waveforms
highlights.reason: The paper presents the first systematic search for eccentric neutron star-black hole (NSBH) binaries using effective-one-body (EOB) waveforms on Advanced LIGO O4 data, demonstrating a ~20x pipeline speedup via multibanding/ratio-filtering and establishing the tightest merger rate upper limits to date.

highlights.title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations
highlights.reason: This paper presents phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar using NICER and Chandra, measuring hotspot thermal properties and testing surface/magnetospheric stability across the 2021 giant glitch.

highlights.title: Tayler Instability and Its Saturation in Rotating Stars
highlights.reason: This work quantitatively constrains the saturation amplitude and radial magnetic field regeneration of the Tayler instability (TI) in rapidly rotating stars, demonstrating that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo alone is inefficient for angular momentum transport, which directly informs core-collapse progenitor spin, proto-neutron star evolution, and neutron star merger remnant lifetimes.

highlights.title: A Spectral-model-independent Diagnostic of Phase-resolved Spectral Convergence in Swift J0243.6+6124
highlights.reason: The study provides a model-independent diagnostic metric to trace the geometry and spectral evolution across critical accretion transitions in the Galactic ultraluminous X-ray pulsar Swift J0243.6+6124.

entries.title: Identifying Scientifically Interesting Galaxies with Vision-Language Models
entries.abstract: Anomaly searches in large astronomical image datasets aim to identify rare objects for follow-up investigation. Yet the objects that are most statistically unusual are not necessarily those of greatest scientific relevance. We investigate whether pretrained vision-language models can directly assess scientific interest from natural-language instructions, enabling galaxy images to be ranked without labeled examples. We evaluate models on a 20,000-image Hubble Space Telescope sample that includes 167 reference anomalies previously identified through machine learning and expert inspection. By scoring images for scientific interest, Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite places 98.2% of the reference anomalies within the highest-ranked ~2,000 images, at a present-day inference cost of approximately $5.05 per 10,000 images. We recover known gravitational lenses, jellyfish-galaxy candidates, and galaxies with visible jets, and release 102 high-scoring candidates for further investigation. These results show that an off-the-shelf vision-language model, without any training on the target data, offers a practical way to rank large image datasets by scientific relevance rather than rarity. The project code is available at https://github.com/TheCheng2005/Galaxy-Anomaly-Search/

entries.title: A GLIMPSE of Dark Matter: JWST Constraints on Early Structure Formation
entries.abstract: While we have a solid understanding of how dark matter (DM) behaves during recombination ($z\sim 10^3$) and in the late universe ($z\lesssim$ a few), much less is known about intermediate times, when the first galaxies formed. These galaxies provide a powerful handle on DM through structure formation, as halos have to exist to host luminous sources. Here we use recent determinations of the UV luminosity function from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) GLIMPSE lensing program, along with legacy Hubble and Subaru data, to test the small-scale behavior of DM during the epoch of reionization ($z\sim 7$). Marginalizing over astrophysical uncertainties, we find the matter power spectrum to be consistent with the cold-DM prediction down to sub-Mpc scales, with 1$σ$ uncertainties of 0.2 dex at $k=3-9 \, \rm Mpc^{-1}$ and 0.5 dex at $k=9-27 \, \rm Mpc^{-1}$, the smallest scales probed at these early times. For thermal-relic warm DM we constrain $m_{\rm WDM} > 3.2\, \rm keV$ (95% CL), independent of lower-$z$ probes. Our results test small-scale structure formation in a new redshift window and demonstrate the promise of JWST to constrain the nature of DM.

entries.title: Seeing Unseen Gravitational Wave Inspirals at the Galactic Center
entries.abstract: The Galactic Center is expected to host a population of extremely large mass-ratio inspirals (X-MRIs) migrating toward the supermassive black hole. We propose an observational approach utilizing the secular gravitational torque exerted by X-MRIs on the highly eccentric S-star S301. This approach is intrinsically limited by the stochastic nature of the surrounding stellar-mass black hole cusp. As S301 propagates through this granular medium, it experiences discrete gravitational encounters. Standard orbital fitting procedures inherently assume a smooth background potential; applying them to stochastic trajectories averages these discrete velocity discontinuities into a continuous secular drift. This introduces a systematic bias that mimics the X-MRI precession signal, invalidating traditional mass estimation techniques. To resolve this degeneracy, we implement a methodology based on the Wavelet Transform Modulus Maxima method to characterize the local Hölder regularity of the orbital motion. This model isolates the singular discontinuities induced by stellar-mass black hole encounters from the continuous torque of the X-MRI distribution, allowing for detection even when instantaneous accelerations are below the instrumental noise threshold. We demonstrate analytically that S301 is highly sensitive to the interior X-MRI population while remaining dynamically decoupled from the secular influence of the exterior cusp. Combining precision astrometry and radial velocity projections, we establish that a minimal population of two X-MRIs is detectable within a five to nine-year timeframe, allowing us to constrain the presence of an unseen orbiter population prior to the launch of space-based gravitational wave detectors.

entries.title: Thinner Disks Struggle to Launch Jets: GRMHD Simulations of Magnetic Field Generation and Transport
entries.abstract: Relativistic jets are observed in some accreting black-hole systems but not others. In X-ray binaries, jet production is closely associated with geometrically thicker accretion states, suggesting that disk thickness may influence the conditions for jet launching. We investigate this connection using three-dimensional GRMHD simulations of disks with $h/r=0.1$--$0.3$, initialized with a toroidal magnetic field with plasma $β=5$. We find that the magnetorotational instability (MRI) generates large-scale poloidal fields through non-axisymmetric shearing waves, with an additional contribution from axisymmetric induction through stretching by channel-like modes. The resulting mean fields become progressively weaker as the disk becomes thinner. Because these fields regulate MRI turbulence, thinner disks exhibit weaker angular-momentum transport and accrete more slowly than the standard $v_{\rm acc}\propto(h/r)^2$ thin-disk scaling would predict. The magnetic-flux transport velocity remains comparable to the accretion velocity, so weaker field generation and slower transport combine to strongly suppress black-hole flux accumulation at smaller $h/r$. Correspondingly, the thinnest disk ($h/r=0.1$) produces an electromagnetic jet efficiency of only $η_{\rm{EM}}\sim1\%$, while the thickest disk reaches the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state and attains $η_{\rm{EM}}\geq100\%$. Using the measured large-scale magnetic flux distribution and transport velocities, we estimate the time required to accumulate MAD-level magnetic flux. Only the $h/r\sim0.3$ disk reaches MAD in the duration of our simulations, at $t\simeq2\times10^4\,r_g/c$, whereas for $h/r=0.1$ we estimate a timescale of $\sim10^8\,r_g/c$. These results link disk geometry to magnetic-flux accumulation and jet launching, with direct implications for the timescales over which jets can emerge in transient accreting systems.

entries.title: Extreme eccentricity in double neutron stars without exotic physics
entries.abstract: The formation of neutron stars (NSs) underpins astrophysical phenomena from supernovae (SNe), radio pulsars and X-ray binaries to double NS mergers that power gravitational waves (GWs), short gamma-ray bursts and r-process kilonovae. A recently reported double NS (PSR J0653+0443) with record eccentricity e=0.9924 provides a unique laboratory for studying GW emission and orbital evolution, and challenges existing formation scenarios. Here we show that such extreme eccentricities arise naturally -- without invoking exotic conditions -- from standard binary-SN physics: instantaneous mass loss (Blaauw recoil) and natal kicks readily produce e>0.99 for both compact and wide pre-SN orbits. The observed orbit matches three families of kinematic solutions spanning a range of kick velocities and progenitor configurations. Physically motivated priors based on NS spin and pre-SN mass transfer constrain the viable progenitor family, demonstrating that the system is not exceptionally rare. Future proper-motion measurements will tightly constrain its natal SN kick magnitude.

entries.title: Hot off the Stacks: X-rays in Romulus25, Part I - Comparisons to Observations from eRosita
entries.abstract: Recent observations from the from Spectrum Roentgen Gamma (SRG)/eROSITA all-sky survey data have helped to illuminate the hot circumgalactic medium (CGM) around galaxies at Milky Way-masses and above. In our study, we explore the hot X-ray emitting (T \textgreater 10$^6$ K) component of the CGM in over 750 galaxies from the Romulus25 cosmological simulation (Tremmel et al. 2017) between 10.0 < log(M$_*/M_{\odot}$) < 11.5. We forward-model soft X-ray [0.5 - 2.0] keV observations of our simulated galaxies using pyXSIM and SIXTE to measure the X-ray surface brightness (SB) profiles of the hot CGM. We then compare the average X-ray surface brightness profiles of six stellar-mass selected sub-samples to compare to the observational results from Chadayammuri et al. (2022a) and Zhang et al. 2024a. Broadly, we find that our stacked SB profiles are too bright compared to observations from Chadayammuri et al. (2022a) and Zhang et al.(2024a) particularly in the inner CGM. Additionally, we calculate the X-ray luminosity (L$_χ$) of the hot CGM for each galaxy and compare the average L$_χ$ across stellar mass to observations from Zhang et al. (2024b) as well as measurements from the EAGLE, TNG, SIMBA simulations. Across stellar mass, the average L$_χ$ of galaxies from Romulus25 are brighter than observations except at the lower, Milky Way-mass end where we are in relative agreement with both observations and most other simulations. We also consider a zero-metallicity emission model, because Romulus25 does not have metal-line cooling, finding the average L$_χ$ decreases by nearly an order-of-magnitude, which better matches observations particularly in the Milky Way-mass regime.

entries.title: Resolving the thermal component of stellar feedback with the "anchor-and-refine" scheme in galactic simulations
entries.abstract: (abridged) Stellar feedback regulates galactic baryon cycles, but galaxy-scale simulations often cannot resolve supernova cooling radii. Momentum-based subgrid models can consequently underresolve the hot gas around young stars. We develop an "anchor-and-refine" feedback scheme that anchors a host cell near each star particle, preventing its displacement and preserving a thermal-feedback reservoir. When the cooling radius is resolved, all supernova energy is injected into the host cell as thermal energy; otherwise, the host cell is refined and terminal momentum is deposited into surrounding gas cells. Idealized tests agree with high-resolution simulations, yielding consistent superbubble properties and preserving hot interiors without artificial cooling. In an isolated Milky Way-mass galaxy, the scheme captures finer X-ray-emitting structures and a sharply defined, X-ray-bright central mid-plane. It also produces a smoother star formation history than pure hybrid feedback. Hot gas dominates outflow mass loading, with the mass-loading factor plateauing at approximately 0.2 at heights z>1 kpc. Phase decomposition indicates that hot gas sustains a steady, energy-driven wind, whereas cooler outflows decline with height because of radiative cooling and gravitational fallback. These results highlight the role of thermal feedback in driving galactic winds. By preserving hot superbubble interiors and the partition of thermal and kinetic energy, anchor-and-refine improves the treatment of hot gas, star formation, and feedback at limited resolution, supporting future applications to galaxy-scale and cosmological zoom-in simulations.

entries.title: Extra! Extra! X-ray Emission!: X-rays in Romulus25, Part II - Physical Drivers of X-ray Emission in the CGM
entries.abstract: Characterizing the hot (T ~ 10$^{6}$ K) circumgalactic medium (CGM) around Milky Way-mass (MW-mass) galaxies is critical to a full understanding of galaxy evolution. In this second paper of the "X-rays in Romulus25" series, we unpack the specific physical processes giving rise to the presence of hot X-ray emitting gas in the halos of galaxies from the Romulus25 (R25) simulation, focusing on L$_{*}$ galaxies. We determine that a strong correlation appears between the mass of hot CGM gas, M$_{gas, T > 10^{5.5} K}$, and the X-ray emissivity, $ε_χ$, measured in the first paper of this series, (Sanchez et al. 2026a, submitted). There is also a secondary correlation between M$_{gas, T > 10^{5.5} K}$ and $ε_χ$ with the average metallicity of the hot CGM gas, $\bar{Z}_{gas, T > 10^{5.5} K}$. We use the well-studied PIONEER simulations from Sanchez et al. (2019), a set of zoom-in MW-mass galaxies run with the genetic modification technique of Roth et al. (2016) and the same physics as R25, to interpret these correlations. We determine that the presence of hot X-ray emitting gas is determined by two key processes: 1) the quantity of hot gas mass in the CGM, M$_{gas, T > 10^{5.5} K}$, is set by the combined total energy injection of $both$ stellar and AGN feedback, and 2) together the average temperature and metallicity of the hot CGM changes the soft X-ray spectrum of the gas resulting in brighter metal-rich CGM and dimmer metal-poor CGM for the same quantity of M$_{gas, T > 10^{5.5} K}$. These results indicate, for the first time, that metal-rich gas halos may bias X-ray observations of MW-mass galaxies.

entries.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
entries.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their hosts stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants as well as chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca ii triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profile characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85-145019.95, a new gas disc system which exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 Rsun to 0.34 Rsun and from 0.54 Rsun to 1.93 Rsun. We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few km to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

entries.title: Not so dead after all: young stars in the massive S0 NGC 3115
entries.abstract: Context: Massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) are traditionally considered "red-and-dead" based on optical observations. However, ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy can uncover a hidden population of young stars with a sub-one-per cent mass fraction. Aims: We measure the young stellar mass fraction in NGC 3115, a massive isolated lenticular galaxy, to test the ubiquity and spatial distribution of this component beyond previously studied ellipticals. Methods: Using SOAR/Goodman spectra and line-strength fitting, we modelled the star-formation history with a single bulk stellar population plus a young component (constant star-formation over the last 1 Gyr). We used ultranest to derive posterior distributions for age, metallicity, [Mg/Fe], and the young stellar mass fraction. Results: By tracking spatial variations in U-band indices, we found the young stellar mass fraction peaks at $0.69^{+0.09}_{-0.15}\%$ in the centre, dropping to zero beyond 1 kpc. This young component correlates with kinematic structures, dominating in the pressure-supported region. We interpret this as residual central star formation fueled by internal processes, such as recycled stellar material. Alternative UV-bright models (e.g., extreme horizontal branch stars) yielded poorer fits and unphysically high mass fractions. Conclusions: Young stars in old, "red-and-dead" galaxies are more common than expected. Their presence across various ETGs with similar gradients indicates that residual star formation is a ubiquitous feature, offering key constraints on the baryon cycle in these galaxies.

entries.title: Ejected and Rejected: Strong Scatterings in Dense Star Clusters
entries.abstract: Understanding the evolution of collisional stellar systems is key to predicting both the bulk evolution of dense star clusters and also the rates of tidal disruption events, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar ejections, and other loss cone phenomena. Although a majority of the evolution is dictated by weak, small-angle scatterings, rare close encounters resulting in strong scatterings can sometimes produce qualitatively different outcomes. To systematically determine the astrophysical importance of strong scatterings, we derive the exact differential rate distribution of velocity kicks in isotropic and spherically symmetric distribution functions representing globular and nuclear star clusters, while also deriving the distribution boundaries and approximate rate scalings. We then extend this formalism to derive approximate rates of energy and angular momentum kicks for objects in the nuclear star cluster, and then apply this framework to study (i) ejections and (ii) ``cancellation'' of extreme mass ratio inspirals. We find that ejection rates are complicated in some regimes due to the saturation of the strong kick distribution and the breakdown of the weak limit, likely enhancing the effect of loss cone shielding. We also determine that a sizable fraction of proto-EMRIs will likely be canceled by strong scatterings, highlighting the need for future work to determine to what degree strong scatterings impact the true EMRI rate.

entries.title: Simulation-Informed Dust Masses in Typical $6<z<14$ JWST Galaxies
entries.abstract: Direct detections of dust in typical $z>8$ galaxies remain untenable, despite the presence of dust suggested by rest-frame UV/optical spectro-photometry. Informed by cosmological zoom-in simulations where dust particles evolve on-the-fly, we present a novel method for inferring dust masses in high-redshift galaxies using stellar half-light radii and UV/optical attenuation. Our methods reproduce observed trends at lower redshift, ultimately diverging from Milky Way-based calibration factors by up to $\sim1.5$ dex. We apply this method to observed JWST galaxies from $6<z<14$, and find dust masses in the range $M_{\rm dust}\sim10^3-10^5\,M_\odot$ that are fully consistent with upper limits from ALMA, and suggest an early dust enrichment period by supernovae followed by efficient grain destruction in the hot gas. Future observations may use our tabulated calibration to infer dust masses over a wide range of stellar masses and redshifts.

entries.title: Combining Multiple Incomplete Astronomical Surveys to Estimate Galaxy Flux Distributions
entries.abstract: In astrophysics, the distributions of fluxes or intensities of populations of sources provide insight into the structure and evolution of the universe. We propose a science-driven hierarchical Bayesian framework to estimate the X-ray flux distribution of a population of galaxies. The distribution is parameterized via a broken power law model, formulated as a mixture of Pareto distributions, and is fit using data from a combination of non-representative X-ray and optical surveys. Because fainter sources are less likely to be detected, astronomical surveys suffer from incompleteness at the low-intensity end, and dedicated survey simulations are used to study the resulting missing-data pattern and determine the form of corrections. We introduce a methodology to combine data from two (or more) surveys with different incompleteness functions. This allows us to leverage deeper surveys (e.g., optical) to more fully characterize the X-ray log(N)-log(S) (where fewer sources are detected). We take advantage of a well-calibrated characterization of the missing-data pattern, particularly in X-ray surveys, to make incompleteness corrections for sources that are not detected in either survey. The proposed model is validated using a simulation study designed to mimic the Chandra Deep Field South (CDF-S), demonstrating accurate recovery of the flux distribution even under high proportions of systematic incompleteness. Finally, we apply our proposed method to data from the CDF-S.

entries.title: No Significant Excess in Typical Variability in CLAS+ Changing-Look AGN Candidates in Rubin DP2
entries.abstract: Rubin Data Preview 2 (DP2) samples the CLAS+ changing-look AGN (CLAGN) candidates $\sim1,000-9,000$ days after their comparison epochs, so it can test whether these objects retain enhanced short-term optical variability after their spectral transitions. Comparing peak-to-peak amplitude in magnitudes against a photometrically quiescent quasar control, one band at a time, we do not detect a significant median-amplitude excess for any state (turn-on, turn-off, intermediate) in either of two bands, nor a different in the median $\,|\,Δ\text{mag}\,|\,$ as function of time lag. The $r$-band CLAS+ amplitude distributions are wider than the control's, with the intermediate state formally significant after multiple-comparison correction. This could hint for a high-amplitude subpopulation.

entries.title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
entries.abstract: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are among the primary sites of the rapid neutron-capture (r-)process. In mergers with long-lived remnants, sustained neutrino irradiation raises the electron fraction of the disc wind ejecta, modifying the resulting nucleosynthesis pattern. Yields from numerical-relativity simulations with accurate neutrino transport are needed to quantify the contribution of BNS mergers to the Galactic production of heavy elements and to interpret kilonova spectra. We present and publicly release tracer trajectories and nucleosynthesis yields for eight BNS mergers forming long-lived neutron star remnants, obtained from general-relativistic simulations with M1 neutrino transport, spanning two equations of state (DD2 and SFHo), and a range of total masses and mass ratios. Passive tracer particles following the dynamical and wind ejecta were post-processed with the nuclear reaction network WinNet up to 1 Gyr. The yields and tracer trajectories are available on the MARTINI platform. At 1 day, the production of light and first-peak elements (He, Ni, Sr, and Y) is similar across models and is primarily enhanced by the neutrino-irradiated disc wind. The yields of heavy nuclei vary by more than one order of magnitude, with unequal-mass binaries producing the largest amounts owing to their more neutron-rich ejecta. Our He yields, particularly in the wind, exceed those of recent studies based on an M0 neutrino scheme, consistent with the stronger neutrino irradiation resulting from an M1 scheme. At 1 Gyr, all models reproduce the second and third solar r-process peaks, but differ in the first peak, the lanthanide region, the mass range between the first and second peaks, and the trans-lead region, reflecting the electron fraction distribution of the ejecta and the dynamical and wind contributions. Two equal-mass models provide a close match to the solar pattern.

entries.title: Considering Numerical Relativity Surrogate Models for AGN Channel Merger Dynamics
entries.abstract: Binary black hole mergers (BBH) are currently observed by the gravitational-wave detectors LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA (LVK). A fraction of these mergers are likely to originate in active galactic nuclei (AGN), but the details of the dynamical processes driving AGN channel mergers remain poorly understood. Monte Carlo For AGN Channel Testing and Simulation (McFACTS) is an open-source, public software used to simulate AGN channel BBH formation and evolution with configurable options for exploring various AGN and Nuclear Star Cluster (NSC) parameter options. Within McFACTS, BBH mergers evolve through gas drag and dynamical interactions, ignoring relativistic effects which can influence merger remnant properties. Here we demonstrate in McFACTS the effect of handing off inspiralling BBH to a numerical relativity (NR) surrogate model, which more accurately predicts the masses, spins, and kick velocities of merger remnants. Compared to a simple analytic approach to calculating merger and remnant properties the NR surrogate model is significantly more accurate at predicting remnant spins, which improve $χ_{eff}$ and $χ_{p}$ calculations, and recoil kicks, parameters especially important for higher generation BBH mergers. Our findings show the NR surrogate significantly changes distributions of remnant spins and kick velocities, as well as showing that alternative methods should be used cautiously in future studies. We also outline some simple models which are computationally efficient and can reproduce much of the NR surrogate model results.

entries.title: Validating an X-ray-based method for identifying Fermi blazars
entries.abstract: Context. Blazars are the main population of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) detected in gamma rays by Fermi. However, around 34% of Fermi sources remain unidentified, partly due to their large positional uncertainties, motivating multiwavelength methods to identify possible counterparts. Aims. We evaluate a method proposed to identify BL Lacertae (BL Lac) candidates among unidentified Fermi sources based on their X-ray properties, using Swift-XRT observations. Methods. We examined published optical spectra for an initial sample of 148 X-ray-selected candidates. We found 71 sources with spectra spatially consistent with the proposed associations and reassessed their classifications using standard blazar criteria. We then compared these classifications with the method's initial predictions. Results. Of the 71 proposed counterparts, 80.28% are classified as BL Lac objects and 87.32% as possible gamma-ray-emitting AGNs, supporting the effectiveness of the X-ray-based selection. We also identify four Seyfert galaxies, suggesting that the method is sensitive to this class despite its rarity among gamma-ray emitters. Conclusions. Our results show that X-ray observations are effective for selecting BL Lac candidates among unidentified Fermi sources and support future spectroscopic follow-up campaigns. The high fraction of BL Lacs and AGNs suggests that blazars may account for a substantial part of the unidentified gamma-ray population. The Seyfert identifications also raise questions about the origin of high-energy emission in AGNs not typically associated with relativistic jets, highlighting the need for further multiwavelength observations.

entries.title: Machine learning applications in the heliosphere
entries.abstract: Space weather is the study of the near-Earth impact of the processes on the Sun. In a this era of technology, space weather emerges as a crucial area of study wherein the state of the near-Earth conditions need to be modeled and forecasted. Crucially, the advent of machine learning provides us with opportunities to study this subject in a rather comprehensive manner. In this chapter, we treat the the processes arising from Sun to the impact on the ground as a set of coupled systems, which can be studied in isolation or in a coupled manner. We define these individual systems in terms of their state vector $\vec{S}$, which provides us with an opportunity to define the physical variables determining the system. This also allows us to consider the systems in terms of their observables, obtained through the action of operators as $\vec{O}[\vec{S}]$. In such a formalism, the machine learning algorithms serve as {\it learned operators}, defined generally as inference ($\mathcal{I}$), propagation ($\mathcal{P}$), and emulation ($\mathcal{E}$). Through such a formalism, we present how machine learning helps advance our understanding of the physical systems under study, while also accelerating the development of operational models for space weather forecasting.

entries.title: Simulating and Characterizing Non-Gaussian Small-Scale Polarized Emission
entries.abstract: Galactic foregrounds present a major challenge for cosmic microwave background (CMB) cosmology as their amplitudes exceed the target primordial $B$-mode signal. While small-scale interstellar medium (ISM) emission is expected to be highly complex, current foreground simulations cannot reproduce the filamentary, non-Gaussian features of ISM structure in a stochastic way. To address this gap, we introduce a framework for generating stochastic small-scale foreground emission, using polarized synchrotron observations as an example use case. This method is capable of producing many independent realizations that additionally inherit morphological information from large angular scales. The underlying structural complexity incorporates anisotropic, multifractal, and advected non-Gaussian features that are tunable with a small number of parameters that carry physical interpretations. Because standard power spectra do not describe the complex phase coherence required for the structural complexity, we evaluate the synthetic fields using higher-order statistics, demonstrating that the Minkowski functionals and structure functions partially capture varying degrees of non-Gaussianity. This work lays the necessary foundation for new foreground simulation suites with stochastic realizations of possible non-Gaussian structure.

entries.title: Probabilistic Stellar Mass and Radius Estimation with Bayesian Hierarchical Stacking
entries.abstract: Accurate stellar parameters are essential for the characterisation of exoplanets, yet most host stars lack direct measurements of mass and radius. We aim to predict stellar masses and radii from commonly available observables and to quantify uncertainties and systematic effects in a way that is consistent with stellar observations. By not relying on a single model, we aim to obtain more robust predictive distributions and reduce sensitivity to model misspecification and outliers. We develop a Bayesian machine-learning framework that combines three probabilistic models through Bayesian hierarchical stacking (BHS): a Bayesian additive regression tree model, a two-process heteroscedastic sparse Gaussian process, and a hierarchical Bayesian neural network. The method propagates measurement uncertainties, accounts for correlations among inputs, and aggregates model variance into final predictive distributions. On a held-out test set the method attains a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 3.5% for mass and 2.1% for radius, improving on empirical-relation-based methods and standard machine-learning baselines. For 44 Kepler LEGACY stars, the BHS masses differ from estimates obtained with the BAyesian STellar Algorithm (BASTA) by a MARD of 4.8%, compared with 8.5% between the empirical relations and BASTA. Applied to about 2400 exoplanet host stars, the predictions differ from literature values by a MARD of 2.7% in both mass and radius. Residual analysis reveals mild underestimation for cool dwarfs, consistent with sparse training coverage, and positive offsets near the main-sequence turn-off that may reflect priors in isochrone-based catalogues. Internal consistency with g = GM/R^2 is greater for the BHS predictions, with a scatter in Delta log g lower by a factor of three than that of the literature values.

entries.title: The Carousel Lens III: Joint lens convergence and source kinematic modeling
entries.abstract: We introduce a new, independent modeling component to the Carousel Lens series by exploiting the spatially-resolved kinematics contained within the lensed arcs, which so far has remained rather underexplored in strong-lensing analyses. We present an end-to-end forward-modeling framework that reconstructs an integral-field spectroscopic datacube from a parameterization of the lens convergence profile together with the line-of-sight velocity, velocity dispersion, and surface brightness profiles of the unlensed source. The kinematic structure of the source acts as an additional set of ray-traceable markers distributed across every lensed image, inaccessible from imaging data alone. Furthermore, by generating an [OII] emission-line datacube, we isolate a single source redshift and remove lens and line-of-sight light contamination. We apply this framework to deep VLT/MUSE observations of the Carousel Lens, modeling the [OII] emission of the quadruply-imaged star-forming galaxy at $z_{\rm s} = 1.432$ that anchors the system's cosmography constraints. We measure an Einstein radius $θ_{\rm E} = 12.816''^{+0.005}_{-0.007}$ and a logarithmic slope $γ= 1.412^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, tightening the statistical uncertainties on both by roughly a factor of $2-2.5$ relative to the corresponding flat emission-line map model. We find that the source galaxy exhibits a strong rotation, lies confidently along the star-forming main sequence, and has an inferred central black hole mass of $\log M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot} = 7.89 \pm 0.51$. These results establish datacube-level forward modeling as a practical and independent route to traditional image-based lens models in the current systematics-limited regime, and one that extends naturally to this system's other lensed sources and to other lens systems.

entries.title: Search for Eccentric Neutron Star-Black Hole Binaries in Advanced LIGO's Fourth Observing Run using Effective-One-Body Waveforms
entries.abstract: The observation of orbital eccentricity in compact binary coalescences would provide a direct signature of dynamical formation environments. Previous matched-filter searches for eccentric neutron star-black hole (NSBH) binaries have been severely limited by computational constraints, necessitating the use of simplified waveform models that capture secular dephasing but omit apsidal precession and inter-orbit harmonics. Including these physical features increases the sensitive search volume for systems with $0.2 \le e_{20} \le 0.28$ by $\sim 25\%$ to $30\%$. We present a rapid matched-filter search methodology that makes the direct use of time-domain effective-one-body waveforms computationally feasible. By multibanding and high-frequency ratio-filtering, our pipeline achieves a $\sim 20\times$ reduction in computational cost. This allows a bank of 88.6 million effective-one-body templates, fifteen times larger than prior eccentric analyses, to search O4a and O4b Advanced LIGO data. We recover the known low-mass mergers GW230518_125908 and GW230529_181500 with parameters consistent with zero eccentricity. Finding no new gravitational-wave events with orbital eccentricity ($e_{20} \ge 0.05$), we place $90\%$ credible upper limits on the local merger rate density of eccentric NSBH systems across the search space of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 7.5\text{-}57\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, up to a factor of $\sim 4$ improvement over previous observational bounds. At the parameters of GW200105_162426, this non-detection establishes an upper limit of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 12.1\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Alternatively, if GW200105_162426 is treated as an eccentric detection, the lack of subsequent detections in O4 updates the inferred local merger rate density of this population to $\mathcal{R} = 6.6^{+6.3}_{-3.8}\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.

entries.title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations
entries.abstract: PSR J0835-4510 (a.k.a. the Vela pulsar) is the best studied pulsar in the Southern hemisphere given its high radio brightness and large glitch activity. However, its X-ray brightness is comparatively lower, making the study of its X-ray profile difficult. We aim to investigate the X-ray emission of the Vela pulsar coming from the surface of the neutron star to infer the properties of its hotspots and assess whether they share a common spectral shape. We also aim to prove whether the 2021 glitch affected the hotspots. We used ephemeris obtained from high-cadence radio observations with the radio telescopes of the Argentine Institute of Radio Astronomy to combine all the NICER observations of the Vela pulsar after its 2019 glitch and before its 2024 glitch. We obtained a folded pulse profile for three different energy ranges and subsequently studied their phase-resolved energy spectra. We additionally analyzed a Chandra observation to quantify the pulsar's contribution to the total soft X-ray emission detected by NICER, which cannot spatially resolve the pulsar from the surrounding pulsar wind nebula (PWN). The pulsar contribution to the total observed emission represents less than 40-45% of the flux below 0.9 keV, dropping to 3-4% in the 0.9-2.0 keV range and further down to ~2% above 2 keV, where the PWN fully dominates. We find that the X-ray folded profile of the Vela pulsar was not measurably perturbed by the 2021 glitch. We studied separately seven regions of the pulse profile. We found that all of them are well modeled by one or two blackbodies. The temperatures of these hotspots are between $0.79(7) \times 10^{6}$ K $\leq T \leq 4.8^{+0.8}_{-0.6} \times 10^{6}$ K, while their sizes vary between $0.048^{+0.016}_{-0.009}$ km $\leq R \leq 3.9^{+0.9}_{-0.6}$ km, and their luminosities between $5\times10^{30}$ erg/s $\lesssim L < 1\times10^{32}$ erg/s.

entries.title: Tidal shells as clocks of galaxy mergers and tests of cosmological models
entries.abstract: Stellar shells-concentric arc-like tidal features formed in galaxy mergers-provide a valuable record of recent galaxy assembly histories encoding both the merger event and the gravitational potential of the host galaxy. We compare shell systems in observations and cosmological simulations from two complementary perspectives. First, we show that simulations predict a substantial population of very large (>100kpc) shells that are rarely observed, revealing a potentially important discrepancy between simulations and reality. Because the scales of observed and simulated shell systems differ significantly, we focus on a comparison of merger histories. Using a shell-identification method, we estimate merger times for a sample of nearby massive prolate rotators and compare them with merger histories derived from cosmological simulations. We also present ongoing efforts to expand the sample of deeply imaged prolate rotators using observations from the Milankovic telescope, paving the way for future studies based on larger observational samples.

entries.title: Evolutionary Demographics of Molecular Ice Mantles in Young Stars with SPHEREx
entries.abstract: Molecular ices are a primary reservoir of volatile C, O, and N in star-forming environments, tracing the chemical pathway from molecular clouds to planet-forming disks. SPHEREx provides contiguous 0.75--5~$μ$m all-sky spectrophotometry for vastly larger samples than are accessible to JWST, enabling population-scale ice demographics for the first time. We present a search for ice signatures in SPHEREx spectra of 20{,}292 young stellar objects (age $<20$~Myr) drawn from the Gaia-based kinematic catalog of Kounkel \& Covey 2019. Using laboratory templates for the spectral signatures of H$_2$O (3.05~$μ$m), CO$_2$ (4.27~$μ$m), and CO (4.67~$μ$m), we identify 746 H$_2$O ice candidates, including 131 high-confidence H$_2$O+CO$_2$ detections and 22 with additional corroborating CO absorption. When binning by age, we find that the H$_2$O$+$CO$_2$ detection rate declines by an order of magnitude between $\lesssim$3~Myr and $\sim$5~Myr, suggesting a chemical or physical evolutionary trend. Candidates concentrate toward high-extinction sightlines ($A_G \gtrsim 2.5$~mag) and embedded SED morphologies, consistent with the idea of envelope dispersal and photodesorption depleting detectable ice mantles within the first few million years of pre-main-sequence evolution. This catalog provides a homogeneous demographic baseline and a prioritized target list for JWST follow-up.

entries.title: Cosmic rays in galaxy halos I: the circumgalactic transport rate and a dynamically significant cosmic-ray reservoir
entries.abstract: Fermi-LAT observations imply that most of the cosmic rays (CRs) produced in normal star-forming galaxies escape from the discs where they are accelerated into the circumgalactic medium (CGM), but the subsequent evolution of those escaping CRs is unclear. Here we construct a simple semi-analytic model for their transport and loss, which we constrain by confronting the model with a series of observations: limits on CR energy densities in the outer Milky Way from Fermi-LAT, the isotropic gamma-ray background (IGRB), stacked CGM X-ray emission from eROSITA, and the requirement that the accumulated pressure of CRs in galaxy CGMs not be so large as to render them unstable. We show that these constraints can be jointly satisfied in only two scenarios: one where CRs diffuse quickly through the CGM and freely escape beyond it into the IGM, and another where the CR diffusion time out of halos is of order the Hubble time. In the latter scenario CRs accelerated by star formation naturally explain both the IGRB and the heat input required to maintain the temperature of the CGM against X-ray cooling, and their relatively slow transport means that roughly half of the CR energy injected into the CGM of an $L_\star$ halo over its star-formation history remains there at $z \simeq 0$. This makes CR pressure dynamically significant, and also means that a non-negligible part of the IGRB is produced by CRs in the Milky Way's own halo. We argue that this latter scenario is the more likely one, as it avoids the need to posit a second source for the IGRB that is coincidentally very close in both power and spectral shape to the contribution from star-forming discs.

entries.title: Tayler Instability and Its Saturation in Rotating Stars
entries.abstract: In stably stratified regions of rotating stars, magnetic instabilities play a key role by enabling dynamo and angular momentum transport. In particular, the Tayler instability of wound-up toroidal fields has long been considered to drive the Tayler-Spruit dynamo. However, the nonlinear saturation of the instability is poorly understood, despite its central role in the dynamo loop. In this paper, we use global simulations to verify the recently completed linear theory of the Tayler instability and determine its saturation. We confirm the picture of overstability of magnetostrophic and inertial waves, which grow on similar magnetostrophic timescales but oscillate with different frequencies. We find that magnetostrophic waves saturate with large amplitudes $δB/B\sim 1$ and dissipate the toroidal field on magnetostrophic timescales, while inertial waves saturate with $δB/B\ll 1$ and erode the toroidal field over much longer timescales. Moreover, magnetostrophic waves efficiently regenerate axisymmetric poloidal fields through nonlinear couplings while inertial waves do not. Our results indicate that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo can operate only through the magnetostrophic wave branch and that its steady-state may follow the scenario proposed by \cite{spruit2002dynamo}, ruling out the small-amplitude saturation scenario proposed by \cite{fuller2019slowing}. Implications for angular momentum transport and magnetic field amplification in evolving stars and nascent neutron stars are discussed.

entries.title: Turbulent gas-rich discs at high redshift: Chaotic orbits and rapid bulge formation at high gas fraction
entries.abstract: Using the \nexus\ N-body/hydrodynamic framework, we show that stellar bars that emerge in high-redshift disc galaxies are different in their orbital characteristics compared to their low-redshift counterparts. We identify bar-supporting orbits and, among them, find the fraction of chaotic orbits compared to regular orbits ($f_{\rm chaos}$). This fraction rises above 60\% for models with $f_{\rm gas} > 60 \%$; for $f_{\rm gas} \lesssim 60\%$, we observe chaotic fractions close to zero. The emerging bars seen in the $f_{\rm gas}= 80\%$ and $100\%$ simulations collapse in $\lesssim$1 Gyr to form central bulges supported by rotation, and this collapse follows soon after the chaotic fraction starts to dominate ($f_{\rm chaos} \gtrsim 50\%)$. Moreover, the gravitational potential in those simulations steepens rapidly over that period, and by integrating the chaotic orbits, we find that orbits that deviate from the evolving mean field are more likely to be chaotic. Hence, we argue that the irregularity associated with the rapidly evolving, central potentials drives higher chaotic fractions in these gas-rich bars. As a result, the emergent bars collapse through `violent relaxation' to form oblate rotating bulges. Supporting evidence for this picture comes from the fact that particles of different mass share identical radial profiles, a natural consequence of the rapid relaxation process.

entries.title: Unveiling the Shock-Excited Molecular Environment in the Orion Protostar HOPS 370
entries.abstract: We present near-infrared K-band ($1.94$--$2.52~μ$m) spectroscopy of the deeply embedded protostellar source HOPS\,370, obtained with the TIFR--ARIES Near Infrared Spectrometer (TANSPEC) on the 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). The spectrum is dominated by prominent molecular hydrogen ($\rm H_2$) ro-vibrational emission, with multiple transitions detected from the $1$--$0$ S, $2$--$1$ S, and $1$--$0$ Q branches. Using the intrinsically linked $\rm H_2$ $1$--$0$ Q(3) and $1$--$0$ S(1) transitions, which arise from the same upper energy level, we derive a visual extinction of $A_V = 23.24 \pm 1.25$ mag, corresponding to $A_K = 2.50 \pm 0.13$ mag, consistent with the embedded Class~0/I nature of the source. The diagnostic line ratio $F(2$--$1~{\rm S}(1))/F(1$--$0~{\rm S}(1)) = 0.12 \pm 0.01$ is consistent with thermal excitation and disfavors ultraviolet fluorescence as the dominant excitation mechanism. Assuming optically thin emission and local thermodynamic equilibrium, we derive an $\rm H_2$ excitation diagram that yields an excitation temperature of $2078 \pm 215$ K and a molecular hydrogen column density of $(1.93 \pm 0.93)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$. We further derive an ortho-to-para ratio of $2.45 \pm 0.21$, indicating substantial shock-driven thermal processing while remaining below the high-temperature equilibrium value of 3. Taken together, these diagnostics indicate that the molecular hydrogen emission in HOPS\,370 originates predominantly in warm, shock-heated gas most likely associated with its protostellar outflow. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combined S- and Q-branch $\rm H_2$ spectroscopy for constraining the physical conditions and excitation history of deeply embedded protostellar systems.

entries.title: A Spectral-model-independent Diagnostic of Phase-resolved Spectral Convergence in Swift J0243.6+6124
entries.abstract: We introduce a spectral-model-independent spectral-shape metric, $δ_{\rm rms}$, to probe phase-resolved spectral evolution in the Galactic ultraluminous X-ray pulsar Swift J0243.6+6124. The $δ_{\rm rms}$--luminosity relation reveals a reproducible convergence--redivergence behavior: spectra from two geometrically opposite pulse phases converge to near identity around $L_{\rm t}^{\ast}\sim8.8\times10^{37}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with a mean shape difference of only $\sim2\%$, and rediverge at higher luminosities, most prominently at higher energies. This strong phase-resolved spectral convergence coincides with a pulse-profile reversal and traces the same transition luminosities previously identified from broadband continuum evolution, including $L_{\rm t}\sim4.5\times10^{37}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$. These results suggest a possible luminosity-driven reweighting between a broadly distributed surface-reprocessed/reflected component and an increasingly important direct accretion-column contribution, while establishing $δ_{\rm rms}$ as a robust, spectral-model-independent diagnostic of radiation-geometry restructuring in bright accreting X-ray pulsars.

entries.title: Age-Resolved Vertical Motions in the Milky Way Warp: A Localized Enhancement in Intermediate-Age Populations
entries.abstract: Determining how the Milky Way warp evolves provides constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of galactic disks. Using Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment Data Release 19 (APOGEE DR19) spectroscopy, we estimate ages for 222,355 red giants. With Gaia astrometry and geometric distances, we analyze 168,824 of these stars in five age bins spanning $0$--$10$ Gyr. The warp-related radial vertical-velocity ($V_Z$) profile of young red giants ($0$--$2$ Gyr) is broadly consistent with those of classical Cepheids and young open clusters. Over $9\leq R<12$ kpc, we find that the mean $V_Z$ values of the intermediate-age red giants ($2$--$4$ and $4$--$6$ Gyr) are $1.48\pm0.46$ and $1.49\pm0.52$ km s$^{-1}$ higher than that of the young population, respectively. By contrast, at $R\simeq12$--$13$ kpc, the $V_Z$ profiles of the $0$--$6$ Gyr red giants are consistent within their uncertainties. The intermediate-age enhancement persists across our robustness tests and may reflect smaller effective kinematic warp onset radii for the intermediate-age populations. The observed velocity differences may arise from the combined effects of earlier perturbations and the present-day warp, or from differences in vertical structure among stellar populations.

analysis.reason: The paper focuses on stellar dynamics of strong gravitational scattering in globular and nuclear star clusters, analyzing EMRI cancellation and stellar ejection rates, which lacks substantive connection to high-energy transient astrophysics topics such as FRBs, supernova central engines, shock breakouts, CSM interaction, relativistic jets, or high-energy neutrinos.
analysis.result: The authors derive the exact bivariate differential rate distribution (DRD) for velocity kicks in isotropic clusters, yielding closed-form DRD solutions for King models and nuclear star clusters (NSCs) with $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$. For extreme-eccentricity orbits ($1-e \ll 1$) in NSCs, strong scatterings at apocenter can impart angular momentum jumps $\Delta J \approx J_c - J$ (where $J_c^5 = \frac{85}{3} \frac{k \sigma(a)^3}{n(a) \langle M_{\rm s}^2 \rangle \ln\Lambda} \frac{G^{7/2} M_\bullet^{9/2} M}{a^{3/2} c^5}$), ejecting compact objects back into the two-body relaxation regime and canceling EMRIs with a scale-invariant rate $N_{\rm CE} \sim \Gamma_{{\rm CE},o} t_{\rm GW} \propto a^0$. analysis.reason: This work directly addresses the physical mechanism of magnetic flux generation, transport, and relativistic jet launching in black hole accretion systems across varying disk thicknesses ($h/r=0.1$--$0.3$) using 3D GRMHD simulations, providing crucial scaling relations for MAD formation timescales and jet power relevant to GRBs, TDEs, and high-energy transients.
analysis.result: Thick disks ($h/r \sim 0.3$) achieve the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state ($\phi_{\rm BH} = 50$) by $t \simeq 2\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ with electromagnetic jet efficiency $\eta_{\rm EM} \ge 100\%$, whereas thinner disks fail to reach MAD within comparable runtimes, giving $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 5$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.1$) for $h/r=0.2$ and $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 3\times 10^{-2}$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.01$) for $h/r=0.1$. The poloidal magnetic pressure ratio and turbulent parameter scale as $\beta_p^{-1} \propto (h/r)^{4.5}$ and $\alpha_\nu \propto (h/r)^{2.5}$, yielding steep transport scalings $v_{\Phi}/V_k \propto v_{\rm acc}/V_k \propto (h/r)^{3.5}$. The required timescale to accumulate MAD-level flux grows dramatically as $t_{\rm MAD} \sim \hat{v}^{-1}(\phi_{\rm MAD}/a_\phi)^{3/(2\xi)}$, taking $t_{\rm MAD} \sim 4\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.3$, $\sim 7\times 10^5\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.2$, and $\sim 10^8\,r_g/c$ (requiring a minimum flux reservoir radius $r_{\rm MAD}^{\rm min} \sim 1200\,r_g$) for $h/r=0.1$.

analysis.problem: Whether geometrically thin and moderately thin accretion disks can self-consistently generate large-scale poloidal magnetic flux from purely toroidal magnetic fields via dynamo processes, efficiently transport it inward to the event horizon, and launch powerful relativistic jets.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional ideal GRMHD simulations executed with the H-AMR code in Kerr-Schild coordinates around high-spin black holes ($a = 0.9$ or $0.9375$), initialized with a purely toroidal magnetic field ($\beta_{\rm ini} = 5$) and cooled via Noble et al. prescriptions to maintain disk aspect ratios $h/r = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$. Analyses employ azimuthal Reynolds decomposition $X = \langle X \rangle + \delta X$ with mean-field induction $\partial_t \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle = \boldsymbol{\nabla} \times (\langle\mathbf{u}\rangle \times \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle + \boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}})$, Fourier modal decomposition of the turbulent EMF $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}} = \langle\delta\mathbf{u} \times \delta\mathbf{B}\rangle$, and magnetic flux advection tracing $v_\Phi = -\partial_t \Phi / \partial_r \Phi$.
assumptions: Initial magnetic field is strictly toroidal with uniform plasma $\beta=5$, containing zero net initial poloidal magnetic flux.
limits: Finite grid resolution in the thinnest disk ($h/r=0.1$) where the strict linear vertical MRI quality factor $Q_\theta^{\rm Jann}$ drops below recommended thresholds ($Q_\theta^{\rm Jann} < 2$) at $r \lesssim 30\,r_g$.

Analytic flux advection trajectories break down near the innermost stable circular orbit and horizon ($r \lesssim 5\,r_g$), and turbulent reconnection of magnetic loops at large radii may erode the available flux reservoir.

analysis.result: The extreme eccentricity $e=0.9924$ ($P=79.1\;{\rm days}$, periastron distance $q=a(1-e)\simeq 0.83\;R_{\odot}$) can be naturally reproduced by an ultra-stripped supernova with an asymmetric natal kick $w\sim 220-350\;{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$ from a pre-SN progenitor helium star of $M_{\rm He,f}\simeq 1.5-2.0\;M_{\odot}$ in an initial orbit $P_0 < 0.10\;{\rm days}$. The theoretical probability of producing marginally bound systems with $e\ge e_0$ under isotropic kicks is analytically derived as $P(e \geq e_0) \simeq \frac{(1-e_0)b}{4k}\approx 0.42\%$, demonstrating that no fine-tuning beyond standard post-SN distributions is required. At gravitational-wave frequency $10\;{\rm Hz}$, orbital circularization leaves residual eccentricity $e\sim 10^{-5}$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar using NICER and Chandra, measuring hotspot thermal properties and testing surface/magnetospheric stability across the 2021 giant glitch.
analysis.result: The pulsed X-ray emission across all pulse phases is best described by thermal components (single or double blackbody models) rather than non-thermal power laws. The inferred hotspot temperatures span $0.79(7) \times 10^{6}\,\mathrm{K} \leq T \leq 4.8^{+0.8}_{-0.6} \times 10^{6}\,\mathrm{K}$ with emission radii ranging from $0.048^{+0.016}_{-0.009}\,\mathrm{km} \leq R \leq 3.9^{+0.9}_{-0.6}\,\mathrm{km}$ and luminosities bounded within $5 \times 10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}} \lesssim L < 1 \times 10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. No significant variation in pulse profile is detected across the 2021 giant glitch ($\chi^2 = 228.43$ for $\mathrm{dof}=255$).
analysis.problem: Disentangling the intrinsic pulsed surface thermal emission of the Vela pulsar from severe contamination by its surrounding bright pulsar wind nebula (PWN) in non-imaging NICER observations, and determining whether giant glitches alter surface magnetic topology or hotspot heating.
analysis.method: Combined high-cadence radio timing from IAR (MJD 58522–60428) via PRESTO/TEMPO2 to fold 321 NICER observations ($530.8\,\mathrm{ks}$ total net exposure) with Chandra ACIS imaging spectroscopy (ObsID 24711, $61\,\mathrm{ks}$) to spatially decouple the pulsar from the PWN ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (0.037 \pm 0.013) \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, $kT_{\mathrm{apec}} \approx 0.21\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{PWN}} \approx 1.56$), followed by phase-resolved spectral fitting across 7 phase bins using the off-pulse phase (0.68–0.72) as background.
limits: The pulsar represents less than $40\text{--}45\%$ of total counts below $0.9\,\mathrm{keV}$, dropping to $3\text{--}4\%$ at $0.9\text{--}2.0\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $\sim 2\%$ above $2\,\mathrm{keV}$, where the PWN heavily dominates.

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively constrains the saturation amplitude and radial magnetic field regeneration of the Tayler instability (TI) in rapidly rotating stars, demonstrating that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo alone is inefficient for angular momentum transport, which directly informs core-collapse progenitor spin, proto-neutron star evolution, and neutron star merger remnant lifetimes.
analysis.result: The Tayler instability in rotating stars ($2\Omega > \omega_{\rm A}$) saturates differently depending on the diffusive excitation mode: magnetostrophic waves (MW, mediated by thermal or viscous diffusion $k_\kappa, k_\nu$) saturate at large magnetic amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \sim 1$ with radial velocity $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$ and regenerate an axisymmetric radial field $\overline{B}_r/B_0 \sim (k_{\rm TI} R)^{-1}$, whereas inertial waves (IW, mediated by magnetic diffusion $k_\eta$) undergo secondary parametric instabilities saturating at much weaker amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-2} \ll 1$ and $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$.
analysis.reading_entry: IV Nonlinear saturation of the rotating TI
analysis.problem: Resolving whether the nonlinearly saturated Tayler instability in rotating stellar radiative zones saturates at large displacement amplitudes (Fuller et al. 2019 model) or small amplitudes (Spruit 2002 / Zahn et al. 2007), and determining the scaling of regenerated radial magnetic field $\overline{B}_r$ and angular momentum transport.
analysis.method: Direct numerical simulations of 3D incompressible MHD equations under the Boussinesq approximation using the Dedalus pseudo-spectral solver on a spherical domain of radius $R$ with uniform rotation $\boldsymbol{\Omega} = \Omega \hat{z}$ and a background toroidal field $\boldsymbol{B}_0 = B_0 (r/R)\sin\theta\cos\theta\hat{\phi}$ (Alfven frequency $\omega_{\rm A} = B_0/(\sqrt{4\pi\rho}R)$), isolating $k_\kappa$, $k_\nu$, and $k_\eta$ diffusive modes.
citation_leads: III.1 Review of linear theory: “The unstable wave modes are categorized as either MW or IW based on their frequency (see below).”

IV Nonlinear saturation of the rotating TI: “Saturation stops the exponential growth of the unstable eigenmodes. This occurs around $t\omega_{\rm A}^{2}/4\Omega\gtrsim 35$ in the $k_{\kappa}$ simulation, and $t\omega_{\rm A}^{2}/4\Omega\gtrsim 15$ in the $k_{\nu}$ and $k_{\eta}$”

VI Discussion: “Our results favoring the [[42](#bib.bib48)] model of the TSD imply that the TSD alone cannot account for the efficient AM transport inferred in evolving low-mass stars [[11](#bib.bib46), [14](#bib.bib34)].”
analysis.research_progress: Confirms the linear diffusion-activated TI theory of Skoutnev et al. (2026) and proves that MW-mode saturation stops exponential growth at dimensionless time $t\omega_{\rm A}^2/(4\Omega) \sim 15\text{--}35$, ruling out enhanced small-amplitude TSD variants and validating the large-amplitude saturation regime with modest angular momentum transport efficiency.

Simulations are organized by column and visualized at times $t\omega_{\rm A}^{2}/4\Omega=40$, $20$, and $20$, respectively. Top three rows correspond to different components of the fields normalized to their maximum values. Bottom row tracks the time evolution. MW saturation results in large-scale displacements of toroidal field loops and perturbations with $\delta B\sim B_{0}$, which destroys the initial axisymmetry of the toroidal field as seen in panels (a) and (b). IW saturation is mild by comparison, with $\delta B\ll B_{0}$ and minor distortion of the initial toroidal field as seen in panel (c).

Results for the $k_{\kappa}$, $k_{\nu}$, and $k_{\eta}$ modes of TI are presented in panels (a), (b), and (c), respectively. The colored points show the measured saturated amplitudes of $\delta B$, $\delta B_{\theta}$, $\delta u_{\theta}$, and $\overline{B}_{r}$, with normalizations indicated at the top of the figure. Their theoretical scalings developed in Section V are indicated by the black lines. One can see that the MW instability (panels a,b) and the IW instability (panel c) give different scalings of the saturation amplitudes with rotation.

The MW and IW branches show different saturation-amplitude scalings with rotation.

analysis.reason: The study provides a model-independent diagnostic metric to trace the geometry and spectral evolution across critical accretion transitions in the Galactic ultraluminous X-ray pulsar Swift J0243.6+6124.
analysis.result: Phase-resolved spectral evolution follows a non-monotonic three-stage convergence–redivergence pattern demarcated by two transition luminosities, $L_{\mathrm{t}} \sim 4.5 \times 10^{37} \ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{t}}^* \sim 8.8 \times 10^{37} \ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$. The phase-difference metric reaches a minimum of $\delta_{\mathrm{rms}} \sim 2\%$ near $L_{\mathrm{t}}^*$, indicating phase-resolved spectral convergence (PRSC) where spectra in opposite pulse phases become nearly identical before rediverging at higher luminosities.
analysis.problem: Disentangling whether pulse profile reversal and phase-resolved spectral changes in ultraluminous X-ray pulsars arise from intrinsic beam pattern transitions, continuum model ambiguities, absorption degeneracies, or geometrical reweighting of emission components.
analysis.method: Formulated a spectral-model-independent shape metric over 2–50 keV: $$\delta_{\mathrm{rms}} = \left[ \frac{\sum_i \Delta E_i \left( \frac{f_{1,i} - f_{2,i}}{\bar{f}_i} \right)^2}{\sum_i \Delta E_i} \right]^{1/2}$$ where $f_{k,i} = F_{k,i} / A_k$ is the normalized area fraction for geometrically opposite pulse phase intervals ($\phi = 0.0-0.5$ and $0.5-1.0$), applied to Insight-HXMT observations across the 2018, 2019, and 2023 outbursts covering $L_{\mathrm{bol}} = 7.9 \times 10^{36} - 1.2 \times 10^{38} \ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$.

must_read.text: Thick disks ($h/r \sim 0.3$) achieve the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state ($\phi_{\rm BH} = 50$) by $t \simeq 2\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ with electromagnetic jet efficiency $\eta_{\rm EM} \ge 100\%$, whereas thinner disks fail to reach MAD within comparable runtimes, giving $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 5$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.1$) for $h/r=0.2$ and $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 3\times 10^{-2}$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.01$) for $h/r=0.1$.

key_highlights.title: Extreme eccentricity in double neutron stars without exotic physics
key_highlights.result: The extreme eccentricity $e=0.9924$ ($P=79.1\;{\rm days}$, periastron distance $q=a(1-e)\simeq 0.83\;R_{\odot}$) can be naturally reproduced by an ultra-stripped supernova with an asymmetric natal kick $w\sim 220-350\;{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$ from a pre-SN progenitor helium star of $M_{\rm He,f}\simeq 1.5-2.0\;M_{\odot}$ in an initial orbit $P_0 < 0.10\;{\rm days}$.

key_highlights.title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
key_highlights.result: Light, Fe-peak, and first-peak nuclei are robustly synthesized with total masses $>10^{-3}\,M_{\odot}$ across all models, whereas second-peak, rare-earth, third-peak, and trans-lead nuclei vary substantially by over an order of magnitude.

key_highlights.title: Considering Numerical Relativity Surrogate Models for AGN Channel Merger Dynamics
key_highlights.result: Incorporating the numerical relativity surrogate model (McFACTSsur) reveals that hierarchical remnants exhibit high spins ($2g$ mergers centered around $a_{\mathrm{final}} \sim 0.85$, $3g+$ mergers at $\sim 0.9$) and a broad kick distribution $v_{\mathrm{kick}} \sim [1, 2000]~\mathrm{km/s}$ with a bimodal feature in $2g$ mergers, while average kicks decrease (mean $\langle v_{\mathrm{kick}} \rangle = 119.21~\mathrm{km/s}$) compared to analytic models ($\n127.17~\mathrm{km/s}$), and higher-generation effective spins shift to $\chi_{\rm eff} \in [0.5, 0.95]$.
